sections.label: SkillsFuture course classification framework
sections.summary: Minister addresses whether a dual-index framework for SkillsFuture courses will be considered, citing existing reports and welcoming industry partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will consider a classification framework for SkillsFuture courses, featuring a dual-index system with (i) a Mobility Index to assess the potential for career advancement of these skills within and across industries and (ii) an Industry Heat Index to gauge hiring trends in booming sectors; and (b) if so, whether the Ministry can collaborate with trade associations to ensure these indices accurately reflect industry demands, and integrate it into the MySkillsFuture portal for users to make informed choices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: These are published regularly so that individuals can make use of the information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For example, the annual Skills Demand for the Future Economy report identifies the priority skills for the green, digital and care economies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In relation to the Member’s suggestion of a Mobility Index, the Skills Demand for the Future Economy report provides information on career transition pathways to help individuals with relevant skills pivot to job roles in these growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Information on hiring demand for these priority skills, in terms of the number of job postings and types of jobs that require these skills, is also provided within the report and as an accompanying Jobs Skills Dashboard, which is similar in intent to the Member’s suggestion of an Industry Heat Index.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: We welcome partnerships with the industry and trade associations, including the Singapore Business Federation, to further improve the signposting of SkillsFuture courses to individuals seeking to upskill.

sections.label: SSG partnerships with trade associations
sections.summary: SSG welcomes more partnerships with business and trade associations and works with sector agencies to make jobs and skills information responsive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In fact, SSG welcomes more partnerships with the business associations and trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Just for information, we work very closely with the sector agencies to identify suitable groups that we can work with so that the information on jobs and skills can be made more responsive and available to Singaporeans who are looking for jobs and skills training opportunities.
